entries.definition: The time a task takes without AI, measured before the start. Without it there is no net effect.
Drafting plus review plus rework with AI, compared with the baseline.
The uneven boundary of what a model does well. Tasks that look similar can lie on different sides (Dell'Acqua et al. 2023).
Sorting tasks by frequency, error cost and checkability to decide what to measure first.
Text that travels with every request, such as project instructions, memory or a system prompt.
The amount of text a model processes per request. Information in the middle of long contexts is used less well (Liu et al. 2024).
Instructions hidden in emails, files or web pages that a model follows as if they came from you.
A tool gets only the permissions its task needs.
The system looks up matching documents and passes them to the model so answers can be supported (Lewis et al. 2020).
A pointer to the source of a statement. It makes an answer checkable, not correct.
A source that was right once and has been replaced by a newer one. A date on every note makes it visible.
The route by which uncertain or faulty cases reach a person instead of being sent.
A person confirms a draft before it leaves the organisation.
The tendency to trust a mostly reliable system and miss its rare errors (Parasuraman and Manzey 2010).
A contract under GDPR Art. 28 when a provider processes personal data on your behalf.
A number or event fixed in advance at which a pilot ends.
